newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius rupee slips vs strong dlr,firms vs pound.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius rupee slips vs strong dlr,firms vs pound.

text.p: The Mauritius rupee weakened against the dollar but firmed versus the pound on Monday, reflecting overseas trends, forex dealers said.
The rupee weakened to a mean commercial rate of 20.0840 against the dollar from 19.9285 on Friday. Against the pound, the rupee was fixed at a mean of 33.4235 from 33.4635 on Friday.
"The dollar is strong on the international scene, and we are following that trend," one forex dealer said.
The dealer said commercial banks continued to be long in their foreign exchange positions as importers' demand remained dull for the first month of the year.

"(Foreign currency) selling intentions can be seen in the interbank forex market, but banks are not willing to buy. And the result is that the market is very quiet. It seems that banks prefer to wait and buy during interventions of the central bank."

During the past few months, the central bank has sold dollars in the interbank forex market during interventions at rates below the prevailing interbank rates. Such interventions were seen as supporting the Mauritian rupee.
Last week, Finance Minister Vasant Bunwaree vowed to follow a strong rupee policy to fight inflation and to create an environment to attract investments.
